line2: OSRS should be fun to play throughout. That means gameplay that is fun in the moment, and rewards your time and effort.
Questing and PvM do this well, but Mining and Smithing do not. These issues are deeply intertwined: If gameplay is fun because it's engaging, it can afford to be more rewarding.
Moreover, Mining & Smithing are not well intertwined with player's journeys, they exist mostly to lock quests behind their requirements.
This update must fix many of the more immediate issues with Mining & Smithing, but even more important is that it sets up Mining & Smithing for success in the game's future.
By giving it a clear identity and purpose in your character's tool kit, and by creating a gameplay framework that is fun and easy to expand slowly together with you, your character and the world.
Many people want many different things. I would like to humbly ask here for some camaraderie.
Even if there's something you don't want, if it doesn't bother you and somebody else would appreciate it, consider letting them have it.
In exchange, I promise I will do my utmost to satisfy every need, desire and more with minimal complexity. I ask also for your trust in doing so.
I have surfaced some ideas for what more complex Mining & Smithing could look like in the Chasm of Fire, both gameplay and integration wise.
But I am deeply excited to share with you also some of the simpler and elegant solutions to long standing problems that are hiding in plain sight.
I hope you look forward to it just as much as I do.

OSRS is proudly "old school", and we know it's important for some players that familiar parts of the game respect their traditional designs, and we aim to do this without holding back innovative new features.
For example, legacy Farming and Thieving methods can coexist in the game alongside newer designs such as the Tithe Farm and the wealthy citizen houses of Varlamore.
We would bear this in mind for any updates to Mining & Smithing.
